title: ADDI object operand skipped ToPrimitive silently breaking date arithmetic
summary: ADDI called vm_to_number directly on objects skipping ToPrimitive. Date plus number silently produced NaN instead of invoking Date toString.
why_critical: Silent wrong values: date plus 0 returned NaN instead of invoking ToPrimitive. Violated ES2020 spec for object coercion. Part of multi-bug ADDI family.
evidence_quote: vm_to_number has no knowledge of valueOf toString Symbol.toPrimitive so date plus 0 fused into ADDI silently produced NaN instead of calling Date ToPrimitive hint default
latency_signal: found while chasing language expressions addition test262 failures; pre-existing in fusion opcode

title: Four BigInt cross-type coercion gaps in falsy/truthy and relational comparisons
summary: is_truthy had no BIGINT case; vm_bigint_relational misread Boolean as garbage and Symbols as bytes; UNM skipped ToNumeric; bitwise ops checked raw operands before ToPrimitive.
why_critical: Silent wrong values in idiomatic code: 0n gave false instead of true; BigInt less than Symbol read garbage; minus Object 1n threw instead of minus 1n. Four independent core gaps.
evidence_quote: 0n gave false instead of true fell through to always truthy default. vm_bigint_relational called get_number_or_fastint unconditionally on non-BigInt operand which reads garbage for Boolean TVal instead of coercing to 1 0. object whose valueOf produces BigInt fell through to plain-numeric int32 path
latency_signal: found chasing language expressions and bigint test262 failures; four related gaps exposed by differential testing

title: ArraySetLength spec violations: wrong coercion order and three bypass routes
summary: Plain assignment skipped second ToNumber call letting valueOf side effects go unseen. Reflect.defineProperty Proxy and Reflect.set bypassed ArraySetLength entirely.
why_critical: Silent spec violations across three API entry points. Side effects flipping writable flag become invisible. Latent null-ctx crash in BuiltinContext.
evidence_quote: Plain assignment arr.length only ran ToNumber once instead of spec ToUint32-then-ToNumber double coercion. Reflect.defineProperty and Proxy DefineOwnProperty fell through generic data-property path silently ignoring exotic algorithm. Reflect.set also bypassing ArraySetLength
latency_signal: pre-existing; only surfaced via deliberate spec-conformance tests hitting all three routes; latent crash never before reachable

title: Arrow function vars hoisted into enclosing scope and missing own-scope for params
summary: Hoist walk entered arrow BLOCK bodies hoisting vars outside. Zero-param arrows emitted no PUSH_VAR so params and body DECLVARs captured parent env instead.
why_critical: Silent scope corruption: arrow with var q declared q outside arrow. Vars accessible from enclosing scope. Found via function_context tests affecting multiple arrow forms.
evidence_quote: hoist_decls walked into arrow BLOCK bodies hoisting vars into enclosing scope. compile_arrow_inner_reparse emitted no PUSH_VAR when arrow had no parameter expressions so param body DECLVARs landed in captured parent env at runtime
latency_signal: found by test function_context.js; affected zero-param and destructured-param arrows

title: Bare for-of into register-cached local left variable undefined in functions
summary: for-of bind emitted PUTVAR env slot but body read from home register; PUTVAR cleared source without updating home breaking register-cached locals.
why_critical: Silent wrong values in common loop pattern: for b of array print b was undefined. Affected for-of and for-await. Pre-existing loop codegen bug.
evidence_quote: for b of 6 7 print b was undefined. PUTVAR updates only env and clears source register so home register never written
latency_signal: surfaced validating for-await LHS parity; worked at top-level only because no register-caching found via test_for_await.js

title: JMP_SEQ JMP_SNEQ offset remapping missing in NOP-compaction broke switch dispatch
summary: New fused jump opcodes missing from NOP-compaction offset-remap switch so branch targets wrong after optimization.
why_critical: Silent wrong control flow: switch dispatch jumped to wrong case after optimization. Only visible via behavioral differential; golden bytecode alone would miss it.
evidence_quote: NOP-compaction offset-remap switch did not list new JMP_SEQ JMP_SNEQ so offsets not adjusted when NOPs removed resulting in wrong branch target broke switch dispatch. caught by behavioral differential that golden files alone would have missed
latency_signal: exposed during jump-aware fusion driver port; behavioral differential and golden-bytecode methodology caught it

title: Cyclic array join recursion causes SIGSEGV
summary: Array.prototype.join recurses on self-referencing arrays with no cycle guard, crashing the engine. Reachable from ordinary code via String(), template literals, and console.log with plain arrays.
why_critical: Memory safety: unguarded recursion causes stack overflow and SIGSEGV. Affects all array serialization paths used in user code.
evidence_quote: Array.prototype.join recursed on a self-reference with no cycle guard, reachable from ordinary code with no console involved. A heap-level join_visited set now bails out.
latency_signal: Found only by testing cyclic arrays directly

title: Proxy own-keys trap use-after-free on garbage collection
summary: Proxy partitioned_own_keys trap result array collected during [[GetOwnProperty]] re-entry due to temproot clear at safepoint. Segfaults on 50+ key proxies under GC pressure.
why_critical: Memory safety: use-after-free of array during iteration. ASAN reports use-after-poison in HObject.array_part; without ASAN causes exit 139.
evidence_quote: The array was reachable only from a C3 local the mark phase cannot see, so it was collected partway through the loop and the next arr.array_part()[i] read freed memory. ASAN reports use-after-poison in HObject.array_part; without ASAN a 50-key proxy for-in under GC pressure segfaults (exit 139).
latency_signal: Silent memory corruption until heavy GC pressure triggered collection mid-iteration

title: Garbage collector marks only innermost scope chain link
summary: Closure scope chain EnvRecord.bindings objects swept because only first link marked. Third link in chain freed while reachable through microtask callback.
why_critical: Memory safety: use-after-poison of EnvRecord.bindings. Silent data corruption until property access crashes.
evidence_quote: an EnvRecord is pool-allocated and never collected, but its `bindings` is an ordinary heap node, and every object-graph marking site rooted only the FIRST link in the chain
latency_signal: Latent defect: only surfaces under ASAN or when microtasks run after GC that collects closures

title: Arrow var hoisting missing, parameter clobber masked by bug cancellation
summary: Arrow block bodies never hoisted var declarations. Separate bug in ordinary functions clobbered parameters when var re-declared them. Two bugs CANCELLED each other in arrows.
why_critical: Two pre-existing bugs masked each other: silent wrong values and inseparable to fix correctly. Fixing one alone broke 11 differential cells.
evidence_quote: In arrows the two bugs had been CANCELLING — the absent hoist could not clobber the param — so fixing the hoist alone turned 11 differential cells newly wrong. Not separable. Three cases fail SILENTLY with plausible values.
latency_signal: Latent: test262 ZERO coverage for var hoisting in arrow blocks; found only by differential test suite

title: Non-escaping break/continue routed through finally unnecessarily
summary: Break/continue in try/catch never leaving the region still routed through finally. VM freed catcher prematurely, swallowing exceptions and running finally blocks twice.
why_critical: Three independent silent wrong answers: exceptions vanished (rc=0), finally ran out of order, and caught exceptions became uncaught.
evidence_quote: Three silent wrong answers fall out of that, all reproduced against node: try { throw e } finally { while (1) break; } e vanished, rc=0
latency_signal: Silent until exception raised in finally block or finally contains loops

title: Unresolved module imports silently bound undefined instead of SyntaxError
summary: Import of non-exported name bound undefined and program completed rc=0. Spec requires SyntaxError at link time before module body evaluates.
why_critical: Silent module linking error: conformance violation across all ES6 modules. Program runs to completion with undefined instead of failing.
evidence_quote: An import of a name the requested module does not export silently bound `undefined` and the program ran to completion with rc=0. ECMA-262 16.2.1.6.2 InitializeEnvironment step 7 makes an unresolvable import an early SyntaxError raised while LINKING
latency_signal: Silent until undefined propagates to observable code; found by cross-checking against spec

title: Suspended generator Catcher chain leak (3.1x memory growth)
summary: Generator abandoned while suspended leaked Catcher per instance plus parked exception. 400k abandonments: 47.6 MB vs 15.3 MB for exhausted loop.
why_critical: Memory leak: only abandoned-while-suspended path leaked; all other generator paths balanced. GC also never marked the chain (use-after-poison).
evidence_quote: Peak RSS over 400k abandonments: 47.6 MB against 15.3 MB for the same generator run to exhaustion, 3.1x; with an Error parked on the chain, 41.9 MB against 9.7 MB.
latency_signal: Latent: only observable under profiling; gc.mark_generator_state never marked gs.cat chain

title: For-in enumeration state leaked on all abrupt exits
summary: break/labeled-break/return/throw inside for-in stranded ForInState. 200k iterations: 112 MB vs 3.7 MB for exhaustion. Also invisible to GC mark phase.
why_critical: Memory leak at every abrupt exit; temproot pinning prevented object reclamation. Masking second bug: mark_and_sweep never marked the chain.
evidence_quote: 200k iterations cost 112 MB against 3.7 MB for the same loop run to exhaustion. Two latent bugs surfaced under ASAN while fixing this: ForInState was invisible to the GC.
latency_signal: Latent: only visible under memory profiling; structurally invisible to GC mark phase

title: GETPROPC2 proxy hop-2 path missing register write-back
summary: Fused two-hop property chain returned early on Proxy path without storing intermediate temp. Proxied receiver invoked with stale value.
why_critical: Observable wrong behavior: o.m.z() calls z with wrong this binding when m is proxied. 15-case differential matrix: 5 wrong before fix, 0 after.
evidence_quote: Observable, not latent: `o.m.z()` leaves the temp live as the call's `this`, so a proxied `o.m` invoked `z` with a stale receiver. The chain-fusion peephole does not check whether that temp is live after the pair — it relies on the VM restoring it unconditionally
latency_signal: Observable when o.m is a proxy and returns an object; otherwise silent

title: UTF-8 decode loop captured multiple characters as single "char"
summary: Object.values('abc') returned ['abc'] instead of ['a','b','c']. The UTF-8 decode loop advanced PAST all continuation bytes including the next character's leading byte, capturing multiple characters in one iteration.
why_critical: Silent wrong value returned without error; affected all exotic String object handling in iteration methods; masked for extended period by exotic_stringobj feature not being exercised in test paths.
evidence_quote: the previous version did `while (data[byte_pos] & 0xC0) != 0x80) byte_pos++` which advanced past ALL leading bytes including the next char's leading byte, capturing multiple characters as a single "char"
latency_signal: Found during Object.values/keys test suite expansion; no test262 coverage initially

title: Array iteration methods silently skipped thrown errors from getters
summary: arr_invoke_getter swallowed thrown errors from accessor getters, returning undefined instead. Affected 12+ iteration methods (reduce, forEach, map, filter, etc.), masking exceptions and producing wrong results instead of propagating TypeError/RangeError.
why_critical: Silent error swallowing in ubiquitous array methods; masked by lack of error-checking in test paths; same bug reached multiple methods across codebase, indicating systemic issue.
evidence_quote: `arr_invoke_getter` swallowed thrown errors from accessor getters (e.g. `Object.defineProperty(arr, "0", { get() { throw ... } })`) — it cleared `heap.has_error` and returned undefined instead of propagating to the surrounding JS try/catch
latency_signal: +276 test262 passes when fixed; indicates wide impact across phases 3/5/6

title: indexOf/lastIndexOf undefined behavior + wrong object equality results
summary: array_strict_equals returned false for all pointer types (OBJECT/BUFFER/POINTER/LIGHTFUNC) including identical heap objects. Also cast (uint)Infinity was undefined behavior, causing timeouts when array length near 2^32 and returning -1 for obj in [obj, obj].indexOf(obj).
why_critical: Undefined behavior on common input (Infinity); silent wrong results for object equality checks; memory-unsafe cast on signed-to-unsigned conversion of infinity.
evidence_quote: `array_strict_equals` returned `false` for OBJECT/BUFFER/POINTER/LIGHTFUNC tags instead of comparing heap pointers... For fromIndex=Infinity, `(uint)(long)Infinity` is undefined behaviour
latency_signal: +49 test262 passes; latent indefinitely in sloppy-mode codepaths; discovered via comprehensive test run

title: Variable parameter name silently clobbered outer binding
summary: Function with parameters but no body locals reused parent's env. DECLVAR for param names then wrote into shared env, silently clobbering outer bindings. `function f(b){} var b = obj; f(1);` would mysteriously change outer b to 1.
why_critical: Silent variable corruption across function scopes; masked by lack of parameter-shadowing tests; violated fundamental JS semantics (parameters are local bindings, not outer-scope mutations); memory/semantic safety issue.
evidence_quote: Its DECLVAR instructions for each parameter name then wrote into the SHARED env, silently clobbering an outer binding when the parameter name matched one in the calling scope. The classic reproducer: isSameValue(b.x, 1) // outer `b` is now 1 instead of the object
latency_signal: Pre-existing latent bug; only surfaced when test suite exercised parameter shadowing

title: Closures could not see let/const in enclosing block scope
summary: Closure's lex_env was always set to freshly-allocated fast_var_env, ignoring captured block-scope bindings. A closure referencing let/const declared in a { block } of parent body would fail to resolve—the fresh function scope had no record of it.
why_critical: Silent name resolution failure masking scope chain bug; affected all closures over block-scoped variables; indicated systemic misunderstanding of lex_env capture semantics.
evidence_quote: closure created inside a function body... the callee's `lex_env` was previously always set to the freshly-allocated `fast_var_env`. That means a closure referencing a let/const declared in a `{` block of the parent body would fail to resolve
latency_signal: Latent in block-scoping implementation; only surfaced when closure over block-scoped variables tested

title: Local variable silently overwritten by property lookup
summary: Expression statement `ok = true` freed the LHS register via free_reg, decrementing next_reg. Next alloc_reg returned the freed slot, letting property lookup (`x.hasOwnProperty("a")`) overwrite the var's value. `_ok` would come back as the string "hasOwnProperty" instead of boolean true.
why_critical: Silent data corruption of local variables by subsequent expressions; memory-unsafe register reuse in register allocator; masked tinycolor module failure.
evidence_quote: expression_statement then freed that register via free_reg, decrementing next_reg past the var's slot. The next alloc_reg returned the freed slot, letting the next property lookup overwrite the var's value with the property-name string
latency_signal: Discovered when tinycolor module mysteriously returned wrong type; pre-existing register allocator bug

title: Compiler hoisting triple-compiled functions causing bytecode corruption
summary: hoist_decls(true) re-processed function declarations already handled by hoist_global_fn_decls, causing triple compilation for modules with many functions. Functions beyond hoisted_fn_names[16] limit were compiled twice, corrupting register and inner function indices.
why_critical: Corruption of compiler state (register indices, inner_funcs array) affecting all large modules (e.g. tinycolor with 37 functions); wrong bytecode generation; systemic hoisting algorithm flaw.
evidence_quote: hoist_decls(true) re-processed function declarations that hoist_global_fn_decls already handled, causing triple compilation... hoisted_fn_names overflowed at 16 entries; functions beyond the limit were compiled twice, corrupting register and inner function indices
latency_signal: Latent until modules with >16 functions; found via tinycolor ESM build failure

title: for(var X=init) in functions created fresh register instead of reusing hoisted slot
summary: For-loop `var X` declared fresh register instead of reusing the one X was hoisted to. Init value and body mutations landed in unreachable register; `return X` after loop saw undefined.
why_critical: Silent wrong return value when for-loop variable pattern used; affected all for-var-loops in functions; masking of hoisting behavior.
evidence_quote: A C-style `for (var X = init; cond; incr)` inside a function declared a fresh register for X instead of reusing the one X was hoisted to, so the init value and body mutations landed in a register the function body never read
latency_signal: Latent in for-loop + hoisting interaction; discovered via module compilation failures

title: Inline cache silently returned stale inherited properties
summary: IC cached inherited property lookups at the owner level. When intermediate prototypes were modified (e.g. B.prototype.foo = ... after b.foo was resolved via A.prototype), IC returned stale value because it only checked owner's prop_alloc.
why_critical: Silent wrong values returned from inherited properties; IC-induced correctness bug; masked prototype chain mutations; affected all property reads with IC.
evidence_quote: The IC cached inherited property lookups with proto=owner... When an intermediate object in the proto chain was modified, the IC returned a stale value because it only checked the OWNER's prop_alloc, not the intermediates'
latency_signal: Latent in IC design; only surfaced when prototype chain mutations tested; wide-reaching impact

title: Uncaught JS exceptions silently converted to VM_ERROR crash
summary: When vm_throw_value returned false (no catcher found), 50+ opcode handlers returned VM_ERROR directly, dropping the thrown value. Engine crashed with 'execute failed: vm::VM_ERROR' + dump; actual exception never surfaced (x is not defined shown as crash instead of ReferenceError).
why_critical: Total masking of exception messages; all uncaught exceptions appeared as VM_ERROR crashes; broken error reporting across entire engine; memory-safety landmine in error paths.
evidence_quote: all uncaught exceptions (x = 1; print(x); → 'ReferenceError: x is not defined' was thrown but never surfaced); the 50+ opcode handlers...just returned VM_ERROR~ directly, dropping the thrown value
latency_signal: Systemic uncaught-exception bug discovered through crash dump analysis; every uncaught exception crashed

title: Strict eval silently leaked bindings into caller environment
summary: Eval assigned eval'd code's var_env = lex_env = caller's env (direct eval). Code's DECLVAR then wrote into SHARED env, mutating caller's bindings. `let x = 10; eval("var x = 99");` mysteriously changed outer x to 99.
why_critical: Silent scope isolation violation; eval could mutate caller's bindings despite strict mode requirements; fundamental ES5 compliance violation; memory/semantic safety.
evidence_quote: builtin_eval...was assigning the eval'd function's var_env = lex_env = caller_act.lex_env... the eval'd code's DECLVAR then wrote into the SHARED env, mutating the caller's bindings
latency_signal: Pre-existing latent scope isolation bug; only surfaced when eval + let-shadowing tested together

title: Array length stored at wrong offset in HObjectExtra, corrupting memory layout
summary: array_len_ptr() returned raw offset into HObjectExtra region at wrong location. struct declared array_length after extra (offset 96) instead of at offset 64 where actually stored. Struct semantics mismatched allocation layout.
why_critical: Memory-safety landmine: heap layout corruption; off-by-32-byte offset error; affected all array length accesses; potential use-after-free or heap corruption depending on allocation patterns.
evidence_quote: array_len_ptr() returned a raw offset into the HObjectExtra region, but the struct declared array_length after extra (offset 96) instead of at offset 64 where it was actually stored
latency_signal: Latent memory-safety bug in struct layout; discovered via Promise state refactor requiring HObjectExtra union reorganization

title: Double-free via GC allocation loop crashes
summary: Periodic GC in Heap.alloc/realloc ran inline mark-and-sweep while objects were held only in C3 locals, causing nondeterministic double-free crashes.
why_critical: Memory corruption: C3 locals with refcount 0 were freed during inline GC before being anchored, violating engine assumption that GC never runs inline in builtins.
evidence_quote: Periodic GC in Heap.alloc/realloc was running mark-and-sweep inline, which could free objects still held only in C3 locals (refcount 0, not yet anchored). This caused nondeterministic double-free crashes in FixedBlockPool.
latency_signal: Nondeterministic flaky crashes found by workers dying in defineProperty tests

title: PUTPROP setter silently corrupts caller local variables
summary: PUTPROP staged setter frame at arbitrary live local registers A..A+3, silently corrupting caller variables on return. propertyHelper broke on every accessor.
why_critical: Silent engine-wide corruption: any code calling setters corrupted function locals. Manifested only with accessors, making it a delayed time-bomb.
evidence_quote: PUTPROP's A/B/C are arbitrary live locals, so invoking any JS setter from inside a function silently corrupted caller variables (test262 propertyHelper verifyWritable broke on every accessor property).
latency_signal: Silent wrong values discovered when test262 uses accessor properties in descriptor tests

title: String concat keys silently fail property access
summary: Non-interned ADD concat results used as keys never matched string table, making map["key_"+i] return undefined after assignment.
why_critical: Silent wrong values: pointer-identity string equality assumption violated for concat results, breaking all dynamic-key object access patterns.
evidence_quote: Fixes concat-key property access bug (map["key_" + i] = v then map["key_0"] returned undefined): non-interned ADD concat results used as property keys were never deduplicated against the string table.
latency_signal: Silent undefined returns; found only via differential testing

title: Double-decref frees Math object prematurely
summary: Overlapping register windows caused decref_callee_regs to release refs but leave stale TVal bits; caller's RET then decref'd same slots, underflowing refcounts and freeing Math.
why_critical: Memory corruption: Math freed and recycled as closure (Math became callable), then double-freed. Manifested as crashes in quicksort.
evidence_quote: Callee frames overlap caller's register window. decref_callee_regs released refs but left stale TVal bits; caller's RET then decref'd same slots again, underflowing refcounts. Math object freed while bound, recycled as closure, double-freed at teardown.
latency_signal: Nondeterministic crashes in recursive quicksort

title: CALL dispatch corrupts VarIC with callee offsets
summary: CALL set ic_base but forgot var_ic_base, causing callee GETVAR/SETVAR to write into caller's VarICEntry array, scribbling garbage misinterpreted as heap pointers.
why_critical: Heap corruption: NaN-boxed fastint values in corrupted vic.key were interpreted as pointers by GC mark phase, causing heap corruption on deep recursion.
evidence_quote: When a callee executed GETVAR, it wrote into var_ic_base[callee_pc_offset] but var_ic_base still pointed at caller's VarICEntry array. Corrupted vic.key fields held NaN-boxed fastint values that GC mark_tval interpreted as heap pointers, causing heap corruption.
latency_signal: Nondeterministic segfault in bench_valstack_copy at specific recursion depths

title: GC mark runs with uninitialized activation fields
summary: Activation incremented activation_count before fields (var_env, lex_env, this_binding) initialized, making incomplete activations visible to GC while holding garbage pointers.
why_critical: GC corruption: mark phase followed garbage EnvRecord pointers left from previous calls, corrupting heap during allocation.
evidence_quote: Incremented activation_count before env_create_function_scope, making activation visible to vm_mark_activations while var_env/lex_env held stale pointers from reused slot. This caused GC to follow garbage EnvRecord->bindings pointers.
latency_signal: Deterministic VM_ERROR on bench_valstack_copy; found in deep recursion patterns

title: Three cascading crashes: array overflow, shape exhaustion, GETPROPC type confusion
summary: Array grow clamped incorrectly (silent write drops for indices 32768+), shape delete recycled root shape causing overflow after 33k cycles, GETPROPC fused numbers as HString* pointers.
why_critical: Three pre-existing landmines masked by each other: silent writes, overflow, type confusion. Each alone silent; together crash bench_object with VM_ERROR.
evidence_quote: Three correctness bugs that caused bench_object crash: (1) grow_array silently dropping writes for indices exceeding ushort max, (2) delete_prop exhausting shape_id limit, (3) GETPROPC casting number constants to HString* producing garbage pointers.
latency_signal: Combined silent failures only surfaced together in heavy workloads

title: Array.length silently accepts NaN, Infinity, negatives
summary: PUTPROP fast path silently truncated array.length without validation, allowing NaN, Infinity, -1, 1.5, 4294967296.
why_critical: Silent wrong values: .length property is fundamental; accepting invalid values breaks all array operations without error.
evidence_quote: Previously `(uint)rc.get_number()` silently truncated, allowing `[].length = NaN`, `Infinity`, `-1`, `1.5`, `4294967296` to all succeed with bogus lengths.
latency_signal: Silent: no error raised; only surfaced when code relied on valid .length

title: Heap.reset leaks stale pointers into freed memory
summary: Heap.reset left error_value, yield_value, iterator_symbol, toprimitive_symbol caches that survived reset and pointed into freed string-table and pool memory.
why_critical: Use-after-free landmine: stale caches pointed to freed memory, corrupting later operations when dereferenced.
evidence_quote: Heap.reset: clear error_value, yield_value, lj.value1/value2 TVal fields and iterator_symbol/toprimitive_symbol HString* caches that survive reset and point into freed pool/string-table memory.
latency_signal: UAF when stale caches dereferenced; manifested in subsequent operations after reset

title: Batch test manifest reader corrupts C heap free lists
summary: Manifest mode pre-allocated 400MB array and loaded via file::load_temp, then iterated inside @pool() blocks. Pool reset invalidated temp memory, corrupting heap free lists.
why_critical: Heap corruption via use-after-free: freed temp memory reused for next allocation, corrupting heap state and causing SIGABRT.
evidence_quote: The pool blocks invalidated the temp memory, corrupting the C heap's free lists and crashing with SIGABRT/SIGBUS (exit 133/134/138/139) after a few tests.
latency_signal: Delayed crashes after heap corruption; deterministic but only after several tests

title: Array.prototype.pop use-after-free via premature string deref
summary: Array.prototype.pop returned a TVal pointing to popped HString then decremented refcount. If only remaining reference was the slot, HString freed and reused, causing garbage reads.
why_critical: Silent memory corruption - string dereferenced while in-flight to caller, reused memory read as Symbol.
evidence_quote: If the popped value's only remaining reference was the slot being removed, refcount hit 0, the HString was removed from the string table, and the freed memory was immediately reused by the next allocation
latency_signal: Silent bug triggered only by specific data patterns; manifested during rosetta suite expansion

title: Object-literal buffer overflow from swapped array dimensions
summary: seen_key_buf declared char[16][64] but guards assumed char[64][16]. Overflow into stack memory caused undefined behavior and nondeterministic batch-runner hangs.
why_critical: Silent stack memory corruption manifested as intermittent hangs, undetectable without memory instrumentation.
evidence_quote: seen_key_buf was declared char[16][64] but the guard logic assumed the opposite: 16 buffers of 64 chars each. Any object literal with a string key longer than 16 characters silently overflowed the inner buffer.
latency_signal: Pre-existing bug manifested as hangs when batch runner hit propertyHelper.js

title: Generator yield* resume_gen capture too late; null-deref crashes
summary: resume_gen save-point was after builtin dispatch. Builtin calls overwrote heap.resume_gen before save, corrupting caller's resume state. Generator re-dispatch crashed on null-deref.
why_critical: Nondeterministic test262 batch-worker crashes from memory safety violation and null-deref.
evidence_quote: vm_call_fn_impl's resume_gen capture was too late. When a builtin runs before Case 3's compiled-function dispatch, it overwrites vm.heap.resume_gen for its callee before the save point, corrupting the caller's resume state.
latency_signal: Found via batch test flakiness; invisible in single-run execution until re-entrant call sequence triggered

title: for-of over generators causes heap corruption from clobbered iterator slot
summary: Generator.prototype.next overwrote caller's this slot during re-dispatch. This slot held generator object for for-of loops; overwriting destroyed iterator reference.
why_critical: Silent heap corruption - iterator object reference overwritten mid-call, breaking loops.
evidence_quote: Generator.prototype.next/.throw/.return overwrote the caller's callee and this slots on the valstack during re-dispatch. The this slot held the generator object that for-of loops reuse for each .next() call; overwriting it destroyed the loop's iterator reference.
latency_signal: Pre-existing latent bug only triggered when for-of looped over generators

title: Megamorphic property cache not cleared on heap reset; false cache hits
summary: mega_cache not cleared on heap reset. Objects reused same addresses/shape IDs as cached entries, causing false hits with stale freed property indices.
why_critical: Silent wrong-value returns from cache serving stale freed indices; intermittent test regressions hard to reproduce.
evidence_quote: The megamorphic property cache was not cleared when the heap was reset between test runs. Newly-allocated objects could get the same addresses and shape IDs as cached entries, causing false cache hits with stale freed property indices and returning wrong values.
latency_signal: Intermittent regression in batch-worker mode; invisible in single-test runs

title: ToInteger silently returns 0.0 on object failure; throw escapes try/catch
summary: builtin_to_integer returned 0.0 when ToPrimitive failed instead of throwing. Also vm.throw_pending stale across calls, causing throws to escape try/catch.
why_critical: Silent wrong-value returns and throw escaping catch boundary via stale VM state.
evidence_quote: builtin_to_integer_vm consumed vm.throw_pending into ctx.should_throw without clearing it, so a stale throw_pending survived into the restarted catch block and misfired on the next opcode, escaping user try/catch entirely
latency_signal: Found only when exception flow tested; silent wrong values in normal execution

title: Peephole fusion loses AND-OR short-circuit result
summary: Peephole fused GE/LE with IF_FALSE to JMP_Nxx. JMP_Nxx does not materialize result. Short-circuit paths skipped assignment, returned undefined.
why_critical: Silent wrong-value returns (undefined instead of boolean) from optimization removing comparison result.
evidence_quote: The peephole fuses the GE/LE with IF_FALSE into a JMP_Nxx, but the JMP_Nxx does not materialize the comparison result. On the short-circuit path the LDREG is skipped, so left ends up holding undefined.
latency_signal: Pre-existing bug invisible unless both sides of AND were comparisons with early short-circuit

title: Peephole bridge-skip logic applied to loop back edges; array corruption
summary: Fused-compare peephole extended offsets to skip bridge IF_FALSE, but applied same logic to loop back edges. This flipped forward short-circuits into backward jumps.
why_critical: Silent corruption of array data and loops; wrong-value arrays and hangs on specific patterns.
evidence_quote: Extending fused_off by that negative offset flipped the fused JMP_Nxx from a forward short-circuit into a backward jump, and the loop either spun forever or corrupted the array via off-by-one indices in swap chains.
latency_signal: Triggered only by specific loop+AND+sort patterns; silent data corruption

title: Template literal parsing corrupts file with nested braces
summary: Template parsing used shared brace_balance counter that drifted on nested constructs. Next brace consumed mid-expression, leaving file remainder unparseable.
why_critical: Silent parse corruption - entire file remainder becomes unparseable garbage.
